turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not afraid of the Mussulmans, nor do I fear your threats, Sandip. My concern is for the well-being of my people and the stability of my land. Your actions are causing unrest and I demand that you cease them immediately.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your concern for the well-being of your people is admirable, Nikhil, but it is also rather quaint. Do you truly believe that your tenants fear the Mussulmans more than they fear you and your outdated notions of propriety?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: My tenants fear neither you nor me, Sandip, but the injustice and oppression that threaten their livelihoods. Your actions are causing them harm, and I will not stand idly by.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, you are so earnest in your outdated ways. But let me assure you, my dear rival, that your tenants are far more enlightened than you give them credit for. They see through the veil of your antiquated rules and laws, and they yearn for a voice, a voice that I am here to give them.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your claims may be convincing to some, Sandip, but they do not change the reality of the harm you are causing. I urge you to reconsider your methods and the impact they have on my people.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And what would you know of their desires, Nikhil? You who live in your ivory tower, blind to the pulse of the people. Let me tell you, my dear friend, the people yearn for change, for a future untainted by the chains of the past.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your assertions may be bold, Sandip, but they do not align with the reality I see on my lands. The people I know fear the uncertainty and violence that could come from your reckless provocations.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And what would you know of the people's hearts, Nikhil? Your eyes are too clouded by the dust of tradition to see the fire in their souls. They hunger for a leader who will guide them into the light of freedom, and I am their beacon.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your words may ring true to those who are misled by your rhetoric, Sandip, but I see the fear and uncertainty in the eyes of my tenants. I urge you to think of the consequences of your actions before it is too late.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, your concerns are misplaced. The people are not your tenants, but the rightful heirs of their own destiny. They yearn for a leader who will guide them, and I am that leader.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not so naive to believe that the people are merely your pawns, Sandip. But your methods are stirring a dangerous brew, one that could boil over and harm those you claim to lead.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, your heart may be pure, but your vision is narrow. The people are not afraid of change, but rather, they long for it. I am merely the catalyst, the lightning in a dark sky, and they are the thunder that follows.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your words may inspire, Sandip, but they also blind you to the reality on the ground. I have come to give you a warning, not to engage in idle debate.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, you speak as if you alone possess the truth. But the world is vast, and so are the dreams of its people. I see the fire in their eyes, the hope that flickers in the darkest night. You would douse that flame with your caution, but I will not be the one to deny them their dreams.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, your warnings come as the cool wind of a distant winter to a flame in the midst of summer. The people are not afraid of the night, but they long for the dawn. Let the preachers preach, let the winds howl, I shall stand as the mountain unyielding to the storm.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I feel caught between their words, each holding a part of my heart. I wish I could bridge the gap between you both.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I understand your zeal, Sandip, but your recklessness endangers us all. I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your words are like the rustling of old leaves, Nikhil, but I am the sapling that reaches for the sun. I will not be swayed by shadows.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your stubbornness is your undoing, Sandip. I have warned you of the danger, and yet you remain deaf to reason.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ... No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
